newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines grounds ageing F-5s after crash.
newsitem.headline: Philippines grounds ageing F-5s after crash.

text.p: The Philippines has grounded its fleet of ageing F-5 fighter jets for inspection and maintenance after one of the aircraft nose-dived into a river bank, killing two people, a military spokesman said Wednesday.

The order by armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera affects the 10 remaining F-5 planes in the air force inventory, most of which were acquired from the United States in the 1960s, Major Eduardo Oban said.
Three were acquired in 1995 from South Korea, he said.
Acedera issued the order after an F-5 jet crashed on Monday during a fly-past ceremony at the Basa air base north of Manila, killing its pilot and an elderly man on the ground.
Oban said it was routine in the aviation industry that "after an accident, all aircraft of the same model or make should undergo a maintenance stand-down for a thorough check-up."
If a crash was caused by human error, the order to ground the planes was usually immediately lifted, he said.

President Fidel Ramos last month officially launched a 15- year plan to modernise the armed forces by signing a congressional resolution appropriating $12.75 billion mainly for the purchases of new equipment for the army, air force and navy and training of personnel.
